data.title: UWM Holdings 3Q 2026: Revenue $811.09M, EPS $0.09 — 10-Q Summary
data.description:
UWM Holdings’ third-quarter revenue declined year over year as lower loan production income, reflecting reduced origination volume, outweighed growth in servicing income and interest income. Net income attributable to the company improved from a loss to income, primarily as other losses narrowed sharply, partly offset by higher expenses and lower revenue.

Financial Highlights

MetricCurrent quarterPrior year quarterYoY change
Revenue¹$811.09M$843.25M(3.8%)
Net income²$55.52M($1.26M)4499.5%
Diluted EPS³$0.09($0.01)1000%

¹ Reported as “Total revenue”. ² Reported as “Net income (loss) attributable to UWM Holdings Corporation”. ³ Reported as “Diluted”.

Business Highlights

  • Loan originations: Volume fell 20.0% to $33.4B from $41.7B, with declines in both purchase and refinance volume as mortgage rates increased.
  • Servicing: Income rose 45.9% to $246.6M, driven by higher retained servicing fees and a larger average servicing portfolio.
  • Servicing platform: About 78% of the portfolio, or $211B of UPB, was serviced in-house as of September 30, up from about 27%, or $66B, at June 30.
  • Capital and liquidity: Issued $1.65B of Series A Preferred Stock and warrants in August; commenced a rights offering in October intended to raise up to $400M.

Original SEC Filing: UWM Holdings Corp [ UWMC ] - 10-Q - Nov. 06, 2026

data.title: Solaris Energy Infrastructure 3Q 2026: Revenue $341.09M — 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Solaris Energy Infrastructure’s third-quarter revenue and earnings rose year over year, led by acquisitions of GESA and Omega and increased deployed power capacity. Growth in Solaris Power Solutions was partly offset by lower last-mile transportation activity in Solaris Logistics Solutions.

Financial Highlights

MetricCurrent quarterPrior year quarterYoY change
Revenue¹$341.09M$166.84M104.4%
Net income²$34.6M$14.55M137.8%

¹ Reported as “Total revenue”. ² Reported as “Net income attributable to Solaris Energy Infrastructure, Inc.”.

Business Highlights

  • Power Solutions: Revenue increased to $284.2M from $104.9M, mainly from the GESA and Omega acquisitions and higher deployed MW capacity.
  • Logistics Solutions: Revenue fell 8% to $56.9M, primarily due to lower last-mile transportation activity; fully utilized systems averaged 104, up from 84.
  • GESA acquisition: Added more than 1 GW of installed generation capacity under operations and maintenance arrangements across domestic and international markets.
  • New contracts: Signed a 7-year O&M agreement covering approximately 400 MW and expanded an energy customer’s capacity to approximately 80 MW from 60 MW.
  • Growth outlook: Secured 15 turbines expected to add approximately 390 MW; total generation capacity is expected to exceed 3,500 MW by the end of 2029.

Original SEC Filing: Solaris Energy Infrastructure, Inc. [ SEI ] - 10-Q - Nov. 06, 2026

data.title: Kirby 3Q 2026: Revenue $977.21M, EPS $2.09 — 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Kirby’s third-quarter revenue and earnings rose year over year, with higher inland marine pricing and increased fuel rebills lifting Marine Transportation results. Distribution and Services also grew, led by stronger power-generation demand and marine repair, while higher fuel costs partly offset marine gains.

Financial Highlights

MetricCurrent quarterPrior year quarterYoY change
Revenue¹$977.21M$871.16M12.2%
Net income²$110.82M$92.5M19.8%
Diluted EPS³$2.09$1.6526.7%

¹ Reported as “Total revenues”. ² Reported as “Net earnings attributable to Kirby”. ³ Reported as “Diluted”.

Business Highlights

  • Marine Transportation: Revenue rose 17% and operating income increased 26%, driven by higher inland term and spot pricing and increased fuel rebills; higher fuel costs were a partial offset.
  • Fleet utilization: Inland tank barge utilization averaged in the low-90% range in the 2026 third quarter; coastal utilization averaged in the high-90% range.
  • Distribution and Services: Revenue increased 6% and operating income rose 13%; power-generation demand and marine repair activity strengthened.
  • Oil and gas: Lower conventional oilfield activity reduced demand for new transmissions and parts, partially offset by electric fracturing equipment deliveries.
  • Outlook: Kirby expects improved financial results in 2026, with KMT demand favorable and power-generation growth and marine repair expected to offset KDS oil and gas softness.

Original SEC Filing: KIRBY CORP [ KEX ] - 10-Q - Nov. 06, 2026

data.description:

Higher same-store base rent from new leases and rent increases, along with lower real estate taxes and non-recoverable expenses, supported property operating income; lower average borrowings also reduced interest expense.

data.title: Helios Technologies 3Q 2026: Revenue $229.7M, EPS $0.53 — 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Helios Technologies' third-quarter net sales and earnings rose year over year, with sales growth across several end markets and higher volume lifting gross profit. Earnings also benefited from the absence of the prior-year $25.9 million goodwill impairment charge and lower net interest expense; higher operating expenses and input costs partly offset the gains.

Financial Highlights

MetricCurrent quarterPrior year quarterYoY change
Revenue¹$229.7M$220.3M4.3%
Net income²$17.6M$10.3M70.9%
Diluted EPS³$0.53$0.3171%

¹ Reported as “Net sales”. ² Reported as “Net income”. ³ Reported as “Diluted”.

Business Highlights

  • Hydraulics: Sales increased 1.1%; excluding the prior-year divested business, sales rose 15.4%, primarily on stronger mobile and agriculture demand.
  • Electronics: Sales grew 9.9%, driven by health and wellness, recreational, mobile and industrial end markets; gross margin rose 40 basis points to 34.7%.
  • Gross margin: Consolidated gross margin increased 10 basis points to 33.2%, as higher-volume fixed-cost leverage was partly offset by component, labor, freight and utility costs.
  • Radio Sound: Helios acquired substantially all operating assets of the audio and electronic products designer on September 8; its results are included in Electronics.

data.title: Post-waterfall recovery needs 1-month recovery window - Nomura's McElligott
data.description:
Investors face continued market "chop" for the next two weeks to one month before a cleaner recovery path emerges following a violent cross-asset liquidation shock this week, according to Nomura strategist Charlie McElligott.

With year-end profit-and-loss pain creating "shell-shock" and slower-moving institutional sellers still working through positions, McElligott advised cash-rich investors with performance runway to look for tactical entry points in battered sectors and potential re-ratings in hyperscalers if capex pullbacks boost free cash flow.

However, finding "sea legs" will take time after a "biblical" wave of systematic de-allocation and forced ETF rebalancing dismantled legacy "high sharpe" momentum trades, McElligott wrote in a note published Friday.

The mechanical selling behind the crash was staggering. Target volatility control strategies dumped an estimated $72B in a single session and $117B over the past week, while leveraged ETF end-of-day rebalancing added another $48.6B of forced selling—a 0th percentile event matched only once in history, McElligott noted. Semiconductors bore the brunt, with levered ETF rebalancing in the sector alone hitting negative $20.8B, followed by $18.3B in broader tech exposure. One-month realized volatility surged to the 100th percentile, amplifying the unwind.

The damage to crowded positioning was comprehensive. The "semis/energy barbell" and "AI enablers vs. hyperscalers" trades cratered, with the latter suffering a 31% year-to-date drawdown and losing 21% over the past month. U.S. momentum factors plunged 24.5% quarter-to-date as "impossible shadow leverage" and "trapped longs" were unwound across passive funds, multi-strat hedge funds, pensions and retail accounts.

Compounding the stress, McElligott added, a surprise drop in the unemployment rate and hot nonfarm payrolls data raised the probability of Federal Reserve rate hikes, with December now 80% priced and cumulative tightening expectations at roughly 50 basis points. "The economic and market 'left tail' just picked up a ton of delta," McElligott wrote.

data.title: Treasuries Give Back Ground Following Stronger-Than-Expected Jobs Data
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - After trending higher over the past several sessions, treasuries showed a modest move back to the downside during trading on Friday.

Bond prices regained some ground after an early slump but still ended the day in negative territory. Subsequently, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its price, rose 2.2 basis points to 4.859 percent.

With the increase on the day, the ten-year yield regained some ground after ending the previous session at its lowest closing level in almost two months.

The pullback by treasuries came following the release of a closely watched Labor Department report showing stronger-than-expected job growth in the month of October.

The Labor Department said non-farm payroll employment jumped by 165,000 jobs in October compared to economist estimates for the addition of 62,000 jobs.

The report also showed employment surged by an upwardly revised 186,000 jobs in August and climbed by an upwardly revised 60,000 jobs in September, reflecting a net upward revision of 84,000 jobs.

The report also said the unemployment rate edged down to 4.1 percent in October from 4.2 percent in September. The unemployment rate was expected to remain unchanged.

'The latest jobs data suggest labor market conditions are tightening, and with inflation well above target, that adds to the case for a December rate hike,' said Michael Pearce, Chief U.S. Economist at Oxford Economics.

He added, 'However, given most of the core inflation overshoot we expect is tied to spillovers from higher energy prices and AI-related pressures, continued falls in tech stocks and oil prices could eliminate the prospect of an additional hike in early 2027.'

Selling pressure waned over the course of the session, however, as treasuries' safe haven appeal provided some support amid uncertainty about the conflict in the Middle East following Democrats' decisive victory in the midterm elections.
